A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARM4R study and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F. Retained, relocated, and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLBench, Kinova, and Franka experiments, training-stage ablations, and qualitative point-tracking results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, a cross-robot control, and quantitative robustness results in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: ARM4R retains the same three training stages, encoders, attention pooling, causal transformer, state-prediction procedure, and L1 objective. The added kinematic argument explains the existing approach; it does not change its algorithm.

E1.justification: Coverage expands within the existing environments: v2 examines the RLBench 'put knife' failure case and tests Kinova cube tasks under object displacement, dim lighting, moving backgrounds, and tabletop distractors. The training datasets, robot platforms, and original benchmark task suites remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands the main 13-task Kinova comparison from ATM and OpenVLA to also include LLARVA and π0-FAST. LLARVA's earlier participation in Tables 1 and 3 is retained and is distinct from its addition here. RVT and RVT-2 are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify cube disturbances at one-third and two-thirds of descent, lighting reduced to 50%, and two nearby distractors. Table 4 adds a Franka control omitting human pre-training. Appendix D.1 describes protocols for the added comparisons, including π0-FAST joint-position control; the original benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial robustness analysis through dynamic-object disturbances and lighting/background/clutter tests in Tables 5–6. It also adds a Kinova-only training control for Franka transfer and failure analysis of unusual rotations and precise insertion. The original training-stage ablations and appendix tracking examples are retained.

E5.justification: The stated five-seed simulation and three-seed real-robot protocols are unchanged. v1 already reports ± uncertainty; v2 uses that format for added results without introducing a new uncertainty definition, statistical test, or stated change in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Original result entries remain unchanged, including ARM4R's 59.47% RLBench and 83.1% Kinova averages. Added results include LLARVA and π0-FAST Kinova averages of 18.3% and 21.2%, the Kinova-only Franka row of 81.3/52.0/73.3%, and Tables 5–6 robustness outcomes. For example, destacking decreases from 94.7% under standard conditions to 74.7% with tabletop distractors.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a kinematic derivation for an open-chain manipulator using products of exponential twist transformations in SE(3). This supplies formal reasoning for the existing geometric motivation. The original point definitions, policy equations, and loss remain unchanged, and no learning or generalization guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The introduction modestly broadens its named comparative contribution to claim superiority over LLARVA and π0-FAST on Kinova, alongside OpenVLA. The abstract, conclusion, and central claims about human-video pre-training and transferable 4D representations remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for failures involving unusual arm rotations and precise insertion. It attributes disturbance tolerance partly to continual action prediction and hypothesizes that attention pooling explains background robustness and sensitivity to nearby distractors. These extend the interpretation, while the existing limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds baseline checkpoints and implementation links, 200-demonstration-per-variation settings, LLARVA's four training epochs, and π0-FAST's absolute joint-position outputs. v2 also adds a project-page link. Existing ARM4R implementation details and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to RVT, RVT-2, and FAST. Related work contrasts RVT/RVT-2's RGB-D point-cloud reconstruction with ARM4R's tracking-based pre-training, and the empirical discussion positions ARM4R against π0-FAST. The broader literature review and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to added explanatory passages, baseline descriptions, and contribution wording. v2 adds conference and correspondence information and places the now-unnumbered Impact Statement after Acknowledgments. The main section organization, abstract, conclusion, and existing limitations text are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds robustness Tables 5–6, expands Tables 2 and 4 with rows, and relocates Table 3. The original training-hyperparameter table is renumbered from 5 to 7. All eight figures are retained unchanged, with local reflow within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The added Franka control better separates human pre-training benefits from robotic-video fine-tuning, while broader baseline comparisons and explicit robustness/failure tests improve empirical support and clarify operating limits. The gains are focused: robustness testing covers three cube tasks, and the proposed kinematic and attention-pooling explanations provide indirect support rather than establishing the transfer mechanism.
